fit: green tea catechins in redox and oncology models
assessment: The review discusses EGCG and tea catechins. Its fatigue example concerns a separate quercetin trial in oncology. No brewed-green-tea fatigue comparison.

fit: coffee polyphenols and an unrelated clinical fatigue question
assessment: Coffee and chlorogenic acid appear in a dietary source list. Fatigue motivates an unrelated quercetin oncology study. No beverage fatigue estimate.

fit: grape procyanidin and Parkinson mechanism review
assessment: Grape is one named source of procyanidin. Experimental antioxidant endpoints and generic rigidity discussion do not identify frozen grape exposure or motor response.

fit: saffron-derived crocin and water-maze learning
assessment: Purified crocin in an experimental aging model supplies memory results. The swimming task measures platform learning. The separately cited mood studies belong to their own samples.

fit: incidental rotarod motor control and clinical fall endpoint distinction
assessment: Table 1 reports an inconclusive acute injected-curcumin rotarod impairment comparison in healthy mice (t=.2988, df=8, p>.05). No measure of Parkinson fall frequency.

fit: developmental exposure to dietary cardamom
assessment: Cardamom feeding during the perinatal period supplies related developmental findings and maze tasks. These outcomes do not measure depression.

fit: coffee metabolites and reported devotional wakefulness
assessment: The review discusses brewed coffee and pharmacology, including a historical ritual-use account. Wakefulness in this setting gives no estimate of Parkinson fatigue.

fit: curcumin intestinal barrier review and linked arthritis comparisons
assessment: The cited pain studies used formulations or combined treatment. The gut-barrier comparison supplies a separate mechanistic route. Ginger denotes a botanical family context.

fit: curcumin gastrointestinal mechanism and exposure differences
assessment: The narrative review describes oral absorption and intestinal hypotheses. It supplies no new separate whole-ground-spice comparison with Parkinson pain.

fit: extra-virgin olive oil in constipation practice advice
assessment: The Parkinson autonomic review lists extra-virgin oil as clinical dietary advice in a group of strategies that it says had not been studied in trials at publication. The cited experimental comparison concerns fermented milk or probiotics.

fit: isolated curcumin and rat stem-cell proliferation
assessment: The study compares cellular proliferation and signaling after isolated curcumin. Neither clinical nor behavioral pain was measured.

fit: crocin review and model-outcome distinctions
assessment: The review covers memory and neuroprotection after crocin. Some settings include depression without a measured depressive symptom after ground saffron.

fit: caffeine withdrawal versus continued beverage exposure
assessment: Fatigue and drowsiness are listed as possible abrupt-withdrawal symptoms. This secondary report neither isolates brewed coffee at usual intake nor gives a Parkinson fatigue result.

fit: multi-herb constipation comparisons involving dried citrus peel
assessment: The synthesis includes 25 trials with 2089 adults and describes Chenpi from Citrus reticulata and C. sinensis. The mixture and modified variants were compared. No peel-only, raw orange or Parkinson-specific result.

fit: turmeric and curcumin as pharmacology examples
assessment: Discusses whole spice and isolated curcumin explicitly. No distinct Parkinson or culinary pain comparison is reported.

fit: coffee in a qualitative arthritis exercise routine
assessment: A participant reports coffee within a medication and exercise routine. Fatigue appears as an exercise barrier in separate passages, without a paired beverage observation.

fit: curcumin and exercise-related muscle outcomes
assessment: The review links curcumin to turmeric and discusses soreness and exercise-related outcomes. No clinical fall-specific contrast for ground turmeric.

fit: broccoli listed as a source of quercetin
assessment: The quercetin section names broccoli among multiple sources. No assignment or observational estimate of steamed broccoli and Parkinson fall frequency.

fit: purified saffron crocin and rat forced-swim immobility
assessment: Thirty rats in five groups. Each injected crocin group had less forced-swim immobility than saline, without a dose order. The 2017 water-maze paper cites it as a separate study.

fit: separate corm fractions and aqueous stigma extract in animal assays
assessment: The author abstract reports reduced immobility with corm fractions and a distinct stigma-extract result. Open-field ambulation was not clearly changed for the reported corm comparisons. Full tables remain restricted.

fit: historical devotional wakefulness account
assessment: The museum publication attributes greater wakefulness during dhikr to brewed coffee in its historical source lineage. There is no direct account of diagnosed Parkinson disease, fatigue comparison or dose.
